title: the true *throughline*
dek: The data does not support inventing another niche. It supports one experience promise: Jen makes people feel informed, protected, and taken care of because the whole move feels handled.

sections.heading: the *correction*
sections.body:
Jen should not perform a crime-scene character, a market-pundit character, or a collection of clever franchises. Her differentiation is the experience of being represented by her: she notices what matters, explains it plainly, protects the decision, coordinates the next step, and lowers the emotional load.

The creative formats can change. The promise cannot.

sections.heading: how one personality becomes a *lead path*
sections.caption: Each surface has one job. The problem was asking every post to do all five.

steps.title: Her life opens the door
steps.note: Personal and feeling-first content earns recognition and reach.

steps.note: She translates the street, number, choice, and tradeoff without performing expertise.

steps.title: Visible care proves the experience
steps.note: Show what she anticipated, protected, coordinated, or removed from the client's plate.

steps.title: Stories let people raise a hand
steps.note: Questions and replies turn private concern into permission for a conversation.

steps.title: DM makes the promise real
steps.note: Send the street, the number, or what changed; Jen takes the next step from there.

rows.claim: Attention is not the primary problem
rows.evidence: Jen generated 197,425 views and reached 38,275 viewers in the 90-day private Insights window. The account is being seen.

rows.claim: Jen's human lens is the strongest discovery asset
rows.evidence: The audited personal/life-first set produced a 161-like median versus 78 for property-first posts, a 2.1× gap. Every bottom-quartile post in the accessible outlier window used the property as beat one.
rows.source_label: Jen outlier audit · accessible post sample

rows.claim: She does not lack proof; she lacks packaging
rows.evidence: Proof or result language appeared in 25 of Jen's 96 public captions (26.0%), versus 19 of 96 for Coffee & Contracts (19.8%). Jen has material to work with, but it is not consistently framed as the experience of being her client.

rows.claim: The lead handoff is the clearest gap
rows.evidence: Only 1 of Jen's 96 captions used an explicit comment CTA. Across the private 90-day window, 1,589 profile visits produced 12 link taps. Content often ends before the viewer is given a natural next step.

rows.claim: Feed posts deserve a bigger job
rows.evidence: Feed posts generated only 3.1% of views but 16.9% of interactions. That is a 5.45 interaction-share efficiency index, directionally suggesting the feed is an underused depth and proof surface.

rows.claim: Local and cultural content creates better conversation than keyword capture alone
rows.evidence: In the 120-comment benchmark sample, local history, neighborhood, architecture, and balanced-market posts produced 60%–100% substantive-comment rates in their sampled sets. The keyword-guide post produced 0 substantive comments and 11 of 15 keyword-only comments.

sections.heading: three angles — one *brand*
sections.dek: These should stack instead of competing. The promise is emotional, the proof is operational, and the CTA is concrete.

items.action: 1. Brand promise — The whole move feels handled
items.why: Best match for Jen's actual service: warm, anticipatory, protective, and low-friction. It is broad enough for buyers and sellers, but must be proven through specific client moments so it does not become generic luxury language.

items.action: 2. Content proof — You'll always know what happens next
items.why: Turns informing and empowering into a repeatable editorial standard. Every useful post should reduce uncertainty, clarify a choice, or show how Jen lowers the load.

items.action: 3. Lead invitation — Send me the street or the number
items.why: Makes the next action feel like Jen: specific, calm, and useful. It can serve buyers now, while seller variants use 'send me what changed' or 'send me the move you're trying to make.'

items.why: It is anxiety-heavy, costume-like, and asks Jen to play a personality she does not have. It also invites professional and brand risk.
The system may use repeatable structures internally, but the audience should experience one Jen—not a menu of branded concepts.

items.action: Stop treating reach as lead proof
items.why: Views and comments are attention signals. A qualified DM, property review, consultation, or client conversation is the lead-path event.

sections.heading: what this still cannot *prove*
sections.body:
The 30-day Insights window sits inside the 90-day window. It is a recent snapshot, not an independent before-and-after cohort.

The feed efficiency number is interaction share divided by view share, not a conventional per-post engagement rate. It is directional.

Post-level saves, shares, qualified DMs, appointments, signed clients, and closed revenue are incomplete. No content angle is yet proven to generate clients.

The promise should be 'the move feels handled,' not a literal guarantee that Jen personally performs every specialist's work.

Local content must remain compliant with fair-housing rules and avoid ranking neighborhoods for protected classes.

meta.positioning_verdict: experience promise + operational proof + concrete invitation
